title: Door lock control experiment (15 subjects, 4 classes, 31 EEG ch)
description: EEG dataset from 15 healthy participants performing a P300-based brain-computer interface task to control a door lock, one of several home appliances. Data were recorded with 31 active EEG channels at 500 Hz using a visual oddball paradigm with four stimulus classes. Each subject completed 50 training and 30 online testing blocks. The dataset supports research on ERP-based BCIs and inter-subject transfer learning.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with an actiCHamp (Brain Products) amplifier using 31 active electrodes placed according to the 10-20 system, referenced to linked mastoids, and sampled at 500 Hz. Participants viewed flashing visual stimuli on an LCD display (stimulus onset asynchrony of 750 ms) in a 4-class oddball paradigm, with Target and NonTarget events. Each subject completed 50 training blocks and 30 online testing blocks with visual feedback.
